business_scope.primary_industry_name: Contract Research Organization (CRO) for Multinational Drug Trials

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Cross-Strait Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA) and its cross-strait trade/investment implementation arrangements
Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation and Taxation Cooperation (signed 2015, not yet fully effective)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Taiwan Company Act (公司法), Articles 20-2 and 22-1 (as amended and effective 2022), imposing the obligation to establish a beneficial ownership register and file it with the Ministry of Economic Affairs; Money Laundering Control Act (洗錢防制法, comprehensively amended in 2018), Articles 5, 9, 12 and 14; Regulations Governing the Approval of Investment in Taiwan by Mainland Area Investors (大陸地區人民來臺投資許可辦法, Investment Commission of MOEA, as amended). Cross-border parent documents are also governed by the Regulations for Cross-Strait Notarization and Authentication.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cross-Strait Notarization Verification via ARATS-SEF (mainland notarization followed by Straits Exchange Foundation verification)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local Market Supervision Bureau in mainland China

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Mainland Ultimate Parent Company, notarized by a mainland Notary Public Office

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, supervisors, senior officers and authorized signatories against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission AML/CFT alerts, and the investment restriction/negative list under the Regulations Governing the Approval of Investment in Taiwan by Mainland Area Investors. Enhanced due diligence is automatically triggered if any UBO holds now or previously held a politically exposed position in mainland China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, or Macau. The AML/CFT risk tier for a Contract Research Organization providing clinical trial management services is classified as Low_Risk_Standard, requiring simplified but not omitted due diligence.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: MOEA Department of Commerce One-Stop Company and Business Registration Portal (商工行政服務入口網 / 公司與商業一站式線上申辦系統)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be registered in Traditional Chinese characters and must contain a distinctive business name together with the business type suffix '有限公司' (Limited Company) or '股份有限公司' (Company Limited by Shares). A romanized or pinyin transliteration may be registered as the English auxiliary name only; the Chinese name remains the primary legal name. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company, and must comply with the Company Name and Business Scope Rules.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name by MOEA Department of Commerce, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the same authority within 15 days of the notice of rejection. If the rejection is maintained, an administrative appeal (訴願) must be filed with the Executive Yuan Administrative Appeals Commission within 30 days after the day the reconsideration decision is served, pursuant to the Administrative Appeal Act. No court action may be initiated before completing the administrative appeal procedure.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted for a Contract Research Organization in the clinical trial management industry. A physical, leased office in Taiwan is required because the entity is subject to statutory licensing supervision by the Taiwan Food and Drug Administration and Ministry of Health and Welfare, and Good Clinical Practice (GCP) inspections require actual operational premises, records storage, and investigative site management capabilities. The MOEA also requires an actual registered address for mainland-invested companies.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 60% likelihood of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first twelve months of incorporation, primarily by the Taiwan Food and Drug Administration under GCP clinical trial audit mandates and by the MOEA Investment Commission in the context of mainland investor pre-incorporation verification, with additional probability if the company engages in multi-site trial coordination.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Companies Act (公司法), Articles 4, 98-100, 128-129, 172, 371, and 387; Regulations on Investment by Overseas Chinese and Foreign Nationals; Regulations for Company Registration (公司登記辦法).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs, Company Registration Division (經濟部商業署公司登記科), acting jointly with the Investment Commission of MOEA for foreign-investment pre-approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Registration Application (公司設立登記申請書) submitted through the MOEA One-Stop Corporate Registration Online System, accompanied by the Foreign Investment Approval Letter (投資核准函), Articles of Incorporation, and CPA capital verification report.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital under the amended Companies Act; the capital must be reasonably adequate for the declared CRO business scope. The foreign investor's funds must be remitted to a Taiwan foreign-currency account and verified by a Taiwan CPA in a statutory capital verification report (資本額查核簽證) before registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board of Directors, convened upon the request of the sole foreign shareholder, unanimously resolved that: (1) the Articles of Incorporation presented at this meeting are adopted in their final form; (2) the subscription for 100,000 ordinary shares, totaling TW$5,000,000 paid in cash by the shareholder, is approved and treated as fully paid-up share capital; (3) the registered office is fixed at [address], Taipei City, Taiwan; (4) [name] is appointed Director and Chairperson, and [name] is appointed Supervisor; (5) [name] is appointed General Manager, with authority over Clinical Trial CRO operations; and (6) the General Manager is authorized to open bank accounts, designate the company seal, and file all incorporation, licensing, and disclosure documents with the Ministry of Economic Affairs.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (Taiwan) - online portal at investcommission.moea.gov.tw
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the foreign investment application together with a CRO business plan demonstrating clinical trial management capacity, proposed capital schedule, and foreign shareholder identity. Obtain the pre-approval letter before filing company registration; the approved capital amount is the ceiling for the subsequently remitted share capital.
required_dossiers: Foreign investment application form (投資申請書)
Business plan covering the clinical trial CRO service scope
Foreign investor's certificate of incorporation or passport, notarized or legalized as appropriate
Investor's audited financial statements or banker's reference letter
Power of attorney authorizing the local agent
Proposed company name, business scope lines, and paid-in capital schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Within 30 days of a deficiency notice, file supplementary clarifications or an amended investment plan; if the objection concerns the licensed clinical-trial scope, re-file after securing a TFDA pre-consultation opinion.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Inspection System (公司名稱及所營事業預查)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in with the foreign investment approval number, search one to three candidate company names, and select the applicable business scope codes covering CRO/pharmaceutical research services. The name reservation is valid for six months.
required_dossiers: Electronic name pre-check application
Foreign investment approval letter reference number
Ranked list of candidate company names (up to three)
Requested ISIC/standard business scope lines
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for conflict or obscurity, immediately re-apply with an alternate name; a written explanation of the rejection is available and can be used to refine subsequent submissions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Articles of Incorporation Drafting and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Independent Taiwan-licensed CPA engaged by the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation to include the registered business scope, share structure, board composition, and CRO licensing requirements. Open a temporary capital collection account, remit the approved foreign currency, convert into new Taiwan dollars, and obtain the CPA capital verification report as required by Companies Act Article 7.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation (公司章程)
Shareholder subscription list and bank deposit certificate
CPA capital verification report (資本額查核簽證)
Director and Supervisor consent letters and qualification statements
Company chop and responsible person chop specimens
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the capital source documentation or revise the articles by a supplementary shareholder resolution; the CPA may issue an amended verification report before use.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Department of Commercial Affairs, Company Registration Division; one-stop filing at onestop.nat.gov.tw
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the establishment registration application with the adopted Articles of Incorporation, CPA capital verification report, first board resolution, registered office lease or consent, and the Investment Commission approval letter. Pay the registration fee; the authority then issues the Company Registration Certificate (公司登記證明書) and the unified business number (統一編號).
required_dossiers: Company establishment registration application form
Adopted Articles of Incorporation
CPA capital verification report
First Board Resolution and appointment minutes
Registered office proof (lease contract and landlord consent, or title deed)
Foreign investment approval letter
Registration fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: When the examiner issues a correction notice, respond within the statutory grace period with the missing by-laws or signatures; the application is deemed withdrawn if not cured within two months, in which case a fresh filing accrues new fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Tax Registration and Uniform Invoice Purchase Permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Taipei), Ministry of Finance, via the same One-Stop Corporate Registration Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the business tax registration that is transmitted electronically to the tax bureau. Obtain the tax registration certificate and apply for the uniform invoice purchase permit; register the electronic invoice (電子發票) mode and select the zero-rated export-of-services treatment for cross-border CRO milestone fees invoiced to foreign sponsors.
required_dossiers: Business tax registration application (營業登記申請書)
Company registration certificate and unified business number
Responsible person identification and tax seal
Registered office lease agreement
Uniform invoice purchase permit application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resubmit missing supporting documents upon tax office notice; if the tax classification of CRO service income is disputed, request a written tax ruling from the National Taxation Bureau before issuing invoices.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Activation, Capital Remittance Verification, and TFDA License Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated foreign-exchange bank; Taiwan Food and Drug Administration (TFDA) for CRO license matters
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open corporate local-currency and foreign-currency accounts using the company registration certificate, chop, and board signatory resolution. File the capital remittance verification with the Investment Commission using bank settlement records. Concurrently submit the TFDA CRO registration application and any per-trial investigational medicinal product import permit requests.
required_dossiers: Company registration certificate and company chop
Board resolution appointing bank signatories
Foreign investment approval letter and bank capital remittance receipt
TFDA CRO registration form and clinical trial SOP manual
GCP compliance statement and AML declaration of the responsible person
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For bank requests, provide supplemental board account-operation resolutions; for TFDA technical objections, correct the CRO quality manual within 60 days and re-submit through the CDE online system.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Health and Welfare (Taiwan), Taiwan Food and Drug Administration (TFDA), Center for Drug Evaluation (CDE), Clinical Trial Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: CRO Registration Certificate (受託研究機構登記證明) under the Good Clinical Practice Regulations for Medicinal Product Trials (藥品優良臨床試驗準則), supplemented by per-trial approvals for investigational medicinal products and IRB/ethics committee clearances

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (Taiwan) (環境部), formerly the Environmental Protection Administration
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full Environmental Impact Assessment; the office-based CRO coordination activity is categorized as a registration-tier administrative service, requiring only bio-safety self-registration for any attached human biological sample storage, with no statutory EIA report or environmental impact statement.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Premises wastewater connected to municipal sewerage must comply with Effluent Standards (放流水標準): BOD5 not exceeding 30 mg/L and COD not exceeding 100 mg/L; no production wastewater generation; biohazardous or investigational medicinal product waste must be disinfected on-site and removed by a licensed contractor under the Waste Management Act (廢棄物清理法); VOC and chemical emissions from any trial sample archive or ancillary laboratory must remain below the Work-Place Air Quality Standards, with acetone TWA not exceeding 200 ppm.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Equipment Inspection Declaration (消防安全設備檢修申報) filed annually with the local fire authority; current Building Use License (使用執照) certifying B-2 office occupancy load; structural seismic compliance or retrofit certificate for pre-1999 buildings; OSHA workplace self-inspection, first-aid and fire-evacuation drill records maintained per the Fire Protection Act; and general workplace safety-and-health monitoring records for the registered office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA), administered through the China National Unified Standard Electronic Tax Service Platform (electronic tax bureau); market-entry registration is coordinated with the State Administration for Market Regulation, which issues the corporate business license bearing the Unified Social Credit Code; cross-border foreign-exchange flows are supervised by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step-by-step for a PRC Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise: (1) incorporate the WFOE at the local Administration for Market Regulation and obtain the business license with the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code; under the 'one license, one code' multi-certificate integration, that code is automatically accepted as the taxpayer identification number; (2) complete initial tax registration with the competent STA sub-branch, electing VAT status (general taxpayer or small-scale taxpayer) and registering for corporate income tax, individual income tax withholding, and stamp duty rolls; (3) activate the electronic tax bureau account and the digital invoice module on the Electronic Invoice Service Platform; (4) open a RMB basic deposit account and, where needed, a foreign-currency settlement account with a domestic bank, and complete the SAFE-related registration so that Taiwan-sourced or other offshore payments may be lawfully received and settled; (5) for cross-border clinical-trial services, file the cross-border taxable service export record (zero-rating/exemption filing) with the STA, attaching the service contract, offshore-consumption statement, and economic-substance explanation; (6) maintain monthly VAT and corporate income tax declarations, digital invoice issuance, payroll withholding, and periodic stamp-duty filings thereafter.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: China does not maintain a check-the-box election; entity classification is statutory. A WFOE nevertheless has elections that materially affect tax identity: (i) general VAT taxpayer vs small-scale taxpayer election (mandatory general status once annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000; voluntary general status is available and is normally elected by a service exporter to access input VAT credits and the zero-rating refund mechanism); (ii) for cross-border supplies where the catalog overlaps, election between zero-rating with input-credit refund and VAT exemption without input recovery; (iii) for hybrid or perpetual instruments, election under the perpetual-bond characterization rules to treat qualifying perpetual bonds as debt (interest deductible for CIT) or equity (distribution non-deductible), fixed for the instrument's life; (iv) election of the 100% R&D super-deduction for qualifying clinical-trial, biostatistics, and data-research expenditure; (v) limited election between actual-accounting and deemed-profit CIT quantification where books are incomplete and STA consent is granted; and (vi) under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement, resolution of dual-residence questions through the competent-authority mutual agreement procedure, including a PE-protective position where Taiwan-side site-management or investigator activities do not create a Taiwan permanent establishment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) - destination-based consumption tax administered under the PRC VAT Law effective 1 January 2026 and its Implementing Regulations, with the Golden Tax IV real-time digital administration framework; statutory rates are 13% for goods, 9% for transport, construction, real estate and agricultural inputs, 6% for services (including clinical-trial CRO management, ISIC 7490), and 3% for small-scale taxpayers (with a temporary reduced 1% levy in designated relief periods); exported goods and qualifying cross-border services apply 0%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory general-VAT-taxpayer registration applies where cumulative annual taxable sales in any rolling 12-month period exceed RMB 5,000,000; CRO service revenue at 6% counts toward the threshold. Below the threshold, election of small-scale taxpayer status (3% levy, no input-VAT credit) is permitted, and a temporary 1% levy applies for qualifying small-scale sales in relief periods. Export-oriented CROs normally elect general status voluntarily even below the threshold because small-scale status bars access to input-VAT credits and to the 0% zero-rating refund mechanism.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates issuance of Fully Digitalized E-Invoices (digital e-invoices) for VAT-relevant supplies; they must be generated exclusively through the official Electronic Invoice Service Platform accessible via the electronic tax bureau. Each digital invoice is authenticated at issuance and carries a nationally unique 20-digit invoice identification number; the platform performs real-time fiscal validation of the issuer's registration status, invoice sequence, and transaction data, then feeds the invoice into the Golden Tax IV data lake for automatic cross-matching with VAT returns, customs declarations, corporate income tax returns, and bank settlement records. No physical pre-printing or manual fiscal stamping applies in the fully digitalized regime; fiscal clearance is evidenced by the platform-issued authentication record and machine-readable QR code. Volume issuers must interconnect through government-approved API (tax-enterprise integration) channels for automated issuance, red-letter reversal, and invoice inventory control; web-based manual issuance remains possible for low-volume taxpayers. The WFOE must configure its e-invoice catalog so that cross-border clinical-trial service invoices are marked as zero-rated or exempt export supplies, and must retain the corresponding cross-border filing reference on the invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the cross-border taxable services catalog, a clinical-trial CRO (ISIC 7490; PRC classifications of contract R&D, professional technical services, or business-support services) may claim VAT zero-rating (0% with input-credit refund) or exemption (VAT-free without input recovery), depending on the precise service character. Eligibility conditions: (1) the service recipient is an enterprise or individual located outside the PRC, including a Taiwan sponsor or a foreign pharmaceutical company's Taiwan affiliate; (2) the service is consumed entirely overseas, meaning the cross-border elements of clinical-trial management - site identification in Taiwan, investigator agreements, trial monitoring in Taiwan, biostatistics and data-management deliverables used abroad - do not confer a benefit on a PRC domestic recipient; (3) payment is received from offshore in a permitted currency and is repatriated to the WFOE's domestic bank account within the mandatory period; and (4) the WFOE holds the cross-border service record filed with the STA and issues the corresponding digital invoice. Contract research and development services used abroad, offshore outsourcing of data processing and IT-enabled services, and software or data services supplied to foreign entities qualify for zero-rating where the offshore-consumption test is met; professional-technical and certain management-consulting supplies qualify for exemption only, a distinction that must be assessed against the specific contract drafting. Services performed partly in the PRC (such as domestic data entry) remain eligible only to the extent the offshore-consumption criteria, interpreted under the STA's cross-border taxable services bulletin, are satisfied. The Cross-Strait Tax Agreement provides the residence and permanent-establishment framework for Taiwan-side activities but does not by itself create VAT zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Master CRO / clinical-trial service agreement, signed project work orders, and milestone invoices identifying the Taiwan or other offshore sponsor as the non-resident recipient and the WFOE as exporter of the services

Customs Export Declaration (China International Trade Single Window) for all cross-strait shipments of trial materials, comparator drugs, biological samples, and laboratory equipment, each declared under the correct export customs regime and HS classification

Bill of Lading, air waybill, or courier consignment note for physical exports, plus a certified electronic service-delivery report (platform access logs, data-transfer records) for digital deliverables such as biostatistics files, clinical databases, and electronic case-report forms

Inward Remittance Certificate: bank receipt slip and SAFE cross-border receipts declaration evidencing settlement of the contract consideration within the FX repatriation deadline, with currency, amount, and remitter matched to the invoice

Zero-rated or exempt digital e-invoice (Blue Letter) issued through the Electronic Invoice Service Platform, together with the VAT return schedule and the STA cross-border service zero-rating or exemption filing record

Per-transaction audit substantiation: clinical-trial monitoring and data-management evidence demonstrating offshore consumption, plus contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation where the Taiwan counterparty is an affiliate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Golden Tax IV performs continuous cross-system matching of digital invoices, VAT returns, customs declarations, CIT returns, and bank FX settlement data; any zero-rating claim failing the matching test is flagged for tax-office inspection. Consequences: (i) the claimed zero-rating or refund is denied, the supply is re-characterized as a domestic taxable supply (deemed domestic sale) with VAT recaptured at the applicable rate, and late-payment interest at 0.05% per day accrues; (ii) fraudulent export-refund claims trigger recovery of the full refund plus an administrative penalty of 100% to 500% of the fraudulently obtained amount under Article 66 of the Law on the Administration of Tax Levy and Collection; (iii) criminal liability arises under Article 204 of the Criminal Law for deceptive export-refund claims, carrying up to 5 years' imprisonment for smaller amounts, 5 to 10 years for large amounts, and 10 years to life imprisonment with fines or confiscation for especially large fraud; (iv) the taxpayer's credit rating is downgraded to Level D, restricting invoice quotas, bank-financing facilities, and fast-track export-refund processing for at least two years; (v) SAFE imposes administrative fines and correction orders for unrepatriated export proceeds and unreported overdue foreign-exchange collection; and (vi) because the Taiwan market often involves related clinical-trial affiliates, the tax authorities will also test economic substance, round-tripping, and cross-strait transfer pricing, with retrospective clawback available for the full 10-year limitation period in cases of fraud or concealment. SAFE and the STA monitor the 180-day repatriation deadline for export service proceeds (measured from invoice or service-completion date, with approved deferral registration available for longer commercial terms); invoices for which foreign exchange remains uncollected at the date of the refund application are excluded from the export refund claim, and overdue unbundled receipts must be corrected through a supplemental VAT return with reverse-charge consequences, interest, and administrative penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE). For a mainland China wholly foreign-owned enterprise, SAFE administers foreign-exchange registration, settlement, payment, cross-border remittance, and capital-account controls, while PBOC supervises banking and payment-system infrastructure. Taiwan-related transactions may also require separate bank, sanctions, documentary, and transaction-screening analysis; the applicable mainland PRC regulatory treatment must be confirmed for each payment route.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The renminbi is generally convertible for bona fide current-account transactions, including documented trade in services, subject to bank review, tax and invoicing evidence, anti-money-laundering controls, and SAFE reporting. Capital-account transactions remain regulated rather than freely convertible. Registered foreign-invested enterprises may generally use permitted foreign-exchange capital funds for approved business purposes through designated capital accounts, subject to negative-list restrictions, authenticity review, bank processing rules, and SAFE requirements. Dividend, interest, royalty, service-fee, and liquidation remittances require corporate approvals, accounting and tax support, withholding-tax compliance where applicable, and bank verification. Cross-border related-party payments are subject to transfer-pricing, beneficial-ownership, substance, and anti-avoidance scrutiny. Clinical-trial and CRO receipts should be supported by executed service agreements, statements of work, invoices, milestone evidence, tax records, and evidence that the services are legally permitted within the enterprise's registered business scope and applicable pharmaceutical or clinical-research regulatory framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Mainland PRC rules do not impose a universal statutory requirement that all service-export foreign-exchange receipts be converted into renminbi immediately or at a fixed mandatory ratio. A qualified enterprise may generally retain eligible foreign currency in permitted foreign-exchange accounts and convert it when needed, subject to bank authenticity review and applicable account limits. For service-export receipts, the bank may require the service agreement, invoice, tax documentation, payment notice, delivery or milestone evidence, and transaction-purpose information. Goods-trade export receipts are subject to trade-facilitation, customs, foreign-exchange monitoring, and classified-enterprise rules; specific conversion timing and settlement treatment can differ by transaction and bank. No fixed statutory surrender deadline or mandatory conversion percentage should be assumed for CRO service revenue without confirming the current SAFE circulars, the bank's implementation policy, and the transaction classification. Proceeds must not be routed through personal accounts, unrelated entities, or artificial trade structures.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium for ancillary collection or payment support; low for core operating liquidity. An offshore electronic-money institution or foreign fintech generally cannot replace a mainland PRC bank account, cannot independently conduct unrestricted RMB deposit-taking or domestic settlement, and cannot bypass SAFE, tax, customs, AML, sanctions, or beneficial-ownership controls. Use is potentially feasible through a licensed mainland bank, licensed cross-border payment institution, correspondent arrangement, or approved collection structure, subject to licensing perimeter, data-transfer rules, transaction-purpose verification, foreign-exchange quotas or settlement rules where applicable, and contractual allocation of chargeback and safeguarding risk. Client receipts, payroll, taxes, clinical-site payments, and capital injections should be routed through regulated mainland accounts unless a specific approved payment model applies.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no single nationwide rule requiring every director to attend a bank branch in person for every account opening. Remote onboarding may be available at the bank's discretion, particularly where the legal representative, authorized signatory, beneficial owner, parent group, and source of funds are readily verifiable. In practice, banks commonly require an in-person visit by the legal representative or authorized account operator, verification of the registered office and business operations, specimen signatures and company seals, original corporate documents, and interviews concerning business model, expected transaction volumes, counterparties, countries, payment purposes, and source of funds. High-risk cross-border or Taiwan-related flows may trigger enhanced due diligence, additional interviews, video verification, or refusal of remote onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the registered business scope, CRO activity, clinical-trial services, and actual invoices or payment flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current business licence; articles of association; approved business scope; regulatory permits or filings applicable to clinical-trial management; CRO operating procedures; organization chart; staff and site information; executed master service agreements; statements of work; sample invoices; milestone schedules; and written legal analysis explaining why each service is permitted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership, layered foreign ownership, nominee arrangements, or inability to identify controlling persons.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified ownership chart through the ultimate natural-person owners; passports or identity documents; registers of shareholders and directors; board resolutions; constitutional documents; trust or nominee disclosures; tax-residency information; sanctions-screening results; and a signed beneficial-ownership certification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from an account that is not held by the registered foreign investor or that has no clear economic rationale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign-investor corporate records; capital contribution resolution; investment agreement; source-of-funds statement; audited financial statements; bank statements showing the funding trail; proof of remitting entity ownership; capital-account registration or bank registration evidence; and a written explanation of any treasury-center or intercompany funding arrangement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large, irregular, or unexplained cross-border receipts, especially from multiple jurisdictions or unrelated payers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customer and payer master file; contracts and purchase orders; invoices; service-delivery and milestone records; payment-purpose declarations; tax invoices or tax filing evidence; reconciliation from contract to invoice to bank receipt; expected-volume forecast; and documented sanctions, adverse-media, and counterparty screening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving Taiwan, sanctioned jurisdictions, politically exposed persons, restricted parties, or high-risk financial institutions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full counterparty identification; ownership and control information; transaction rationale; end-use statement; routing-bank details; sanctions and export-control screening; board approval; legal opinion on the applicable cross-border restrictions; and evidence that no prohibited intermediary, goods, technology, or recipient is involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Clinical-trial funds that may be mistaken for patient payments, medical procurement, research grants, investigator payments, or regulated pharmaceutical transactions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Clinical-trial protocol summary; sponsor agreement; investigator-site agreements; ethics or regulatory approvals where applicable; payment-flow map; separation of sponsor, investigator, site, patient, and vendor funds; vendor due diligence; anti-bribery controls; and accounting policies demonstrating that the WFOE receives service revenue rather than holding client or patient money.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, employee accounts, third-party collection accounts, cash settlement, or unexplained intercompany netting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy prohibiting personal or unauthorized accounts; approved bank-account matrix; intercompany agreements; netting policy and reconciliation; exception logs; audit trail; corrective-action records; and evidence of refunds or remediation for any historical deviation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected payment volume, countries, currencies, or transaction types are inconsistent with the enterprise profile submitted during onboarding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-year financial model; country and currency matrix; monthly cash-flow forecast; client pipeline; contract backlog; staffing plan; tax budget; treasury policy; transaction-monitoring thresholds; and management certification explaining seasonal or milestone-driven volatility.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient operational substance or a registered address that does not support the claimed CRO activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease and address verification; photographs or inspection evidence; employee roster; payroll records; social-insurance records; equipment and information-security policies; service-provider agreements; management biographies; regulatory registrations; and evidence of actual project management and quality-control functions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder capital through the WFOE's designated capital account or other bank account permitted for the specific capital transaction, using a remitting entity that matches the registered foreign investor or an expressly documented and bank-approved funding structure. Before remittance, confirm foreign-investment registration or bank-side registration requirements, account status, permitted currency, investment purpose, and receiving-bank instructions. The payment message should identify the investor, beneficiary WFOE, capital-contribution purpose, currency, and relevant corporate resolution or registration reference. Maintain the full audit trail from investor board approval to originating bank, correspondent banks, receiving bank, capital-account credit, and subsequent use. Convert or use funds only for permitted business purposes and retain evidence for SAFE, tax, bank, and statutory audit review. Do not mix capital injections with service revenue, shareholder loans, payroll funds, or third-party collections without documented account segregation and regulatory approval.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use regulated mainland bank rails for supplier, clinical-site, investigator, laboratory, technology, and other business payments. For ordinary commercial remittances, use SWIFT MT103 or the bank's current ISO 20022 equivalent with accurate beneficiary, intermediary-bank, invoice, contract, purpose, and fee instructions. For material cross-border purchases or services, preserve the contract, invoice, tax treatment, delivery or service evidence, and withholding analysis. Commercial letters of credit may be used for eligible goods or document-based transactions, but they are generally less suited to pure CRO service milestones unless the structure is commercially and legally appropriate. Documentary collections, open-account wires, bank guarantees, and escrow arrangements may be available subject to bank approval. Each payment must pass sanctions, AML, foreign-exchange, tax, and underlying-transaction checks. Where outbound royalties, interest, dividends, service fees, or related-party charges are involved, obtain the required corporate approvals and complete applicable tax withholding, reporting, and bank documentation before remittance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable RMB foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized mainland bank, limited to genuine underlying exposure and documented hedging purposes.
Foreign-exchange swaps with an authorized bank where the product, tenor, collateral, underlying exposure, and settlement structure comply with applicable PBOC, SAFE, and bank requirements.
Currency options or option combinations offered by an authorized bank, subject to suitability, risk disclosure, genuine-need review, and prohibition on speculative use.

Non-deliverable forwards may be available through offshore counterparties for permitted hedging of non-deliverable or restricted currencies, but they do not provide unrestricted access to onshore RMB conversion and may create basis, settlement, regulatory, tax, and enforceability risks. Obtain bank and counsel confirmation before execution.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps may be considered for documented debt or funding exposure through authorized counterparties, subject to transaction-specific approvals, accounting treatment, collateral terms, and cross-border borrowing or lending rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May 1 through May 31 of the year following the calendar tax year; extended deadlines available with approved application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and underpayment penalties; surcharge up to 30% of underpaid tax plus daily interest; persistent non-filing may trigger estimated assessment and administrative fines under the Income Tax Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Annual Report (WFOE Operational Declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Investment Review, Ministry of Economic Affairs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by May 31, covering prior calendar year operations and shareholding structure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or false filing may result in administrative fines, review of foreign investment approval, and potential restriction on profit remittance or share transfer under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Individual Income Tax Withholding Statements (Salary, Remuneration, and Dividend Withholding)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By January 31 following the calendar year for all payments subject to withholding made in the previous year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: penalty of 10% on underreported withholding, with minimum NT$15,000; negligence and fraud penalties increase to 20% and 40% respectively.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Bimonthly, due on the 15th day of the month immediately following the two-month filing period; six filings per calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: NT$1,200 to NT$12,000 fine plus 1% monthly interest on underpaid tax; repeated non-compliance may trigger business registration revocation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent CPA audit for non-public companies with paid-in capital exceeding NT$30 million, or where the Financial Supervisory Commission/MOEA requires audit for specific industries or regulatory purposes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (Local GAAP) pursuant to the Business Entity Accounting Act and related regulations; IFRS is optionally adoptable for non-public companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Taiwan Company Act, non-public companies must maintain a register of beneficial owners and file any changes with MOEA within 15 days. No stand-alone annual UBO filing is required if no shareholder or control change occurred; however, the annual corporate secretarial task must include confirmation to directors, supervisors, and shareholders holding more than 10% interest to verify current ownership and ensure any changes have been filed before the annual shareholders' meeting.
